encoded-powershell-execution.title: Encoded or download-oriented PowerShell execution
encoded-powershell-execution.objective: Identify PowerShell commands or event evidence consistent with encoded execution, payload retrieval, in-memory execution, or command obfuscation.
encoded-powershell-execution.selection_guidance: Use when PowerShell, encoded command lines, script-block fragments, download cradles, or suspicious PSReadLine history are present.

artifacts.notes: PSReadLine may be absent, disabled, cleared, or incomplete.
Retain full event payloads in raw evidence.
Use bounded PowerShell and Security log families instead of broad EVTX collection.

expected_signals: EncodedCommand or base64 decoding primitives
DownloadString, WebClient, Invoke-WebRequest, or BITS retrieval
Invoke-Expression or reflection-based execution
PowerShell activity adjacent to suspicious file creation or process execution
caveats: PSReadLine is user- and configuration-dependent.
Encoded PowerShell is not inherently malicious.
Event payload fields can be large and require bounded snippets for review.
scope_expansion_triggers: Same normalized command, URL, domain, hash, or payload path appears on another host.
PowerShell activity is followed by remote service, task, or account activity.

suspicious-service-creation.title: Suspicious service creation or modification
suspicious-service-creation.objective: Identify service installation, executable-path drift, service DLL abuse, or service-based remote execution.
suspicious-service-creation.selection_guidance: Use for Event ID 7045-style evidence, unusual service binaries, service DLL changes, remote administration, or lateral-movement leads.

artifacts.notes: Separate executable path from arguments in derived review output.
Some service fields can be sparse on mapped dead-disk clients.

expected_signals: Service executable in a user-writable or temporary path
Service name mapped to an uncommon executable or DLL
Command shell, script interpreter, or encoded arguments in ImagePath
Unsigned or rare service binary
Service creation adjacent to remote logon activity
caveats: A rare service is not automatically malicious.
Mapped dead-disk service collection may be incomplete.
Hash and certificate fields require Calculate_hashes=Y.
scope_expansion_triggers: Same service name, executable path, DLL, hash, or account appears on multiple hosts.
Service creation follows a remote logon or explicit credential use.

scheduled-task-persistence.title: Scheduled-task persistence or execution
scheduled-task-persistence.objective: Identify malicious scheduled tasks, hidden TaskCache entries, or task actions that launch suspicious commands or binaries.
scheduled-task-persistence.selection_guidance: Use when task names, Task Scheduler events, registry TaskCache anomalies, or recurring execution are present.

artifacts.notes: Field names remain unprofiled and require validation against live output.
Field names remain unprofiled and require validation against live output.

expected_signals: Task action launches a script interpreter or binary from a user-writable path
Hidden task or missing security descriptor
Unexpected privileged principal
Task registration near suspicious file creation or account activity
caveats: Task Scheduler artifact schemas vary by result component and version.
Task names alone are weak evidence.
Registry TaskCache findings require correlation with task XML and execution evidence.
scope_expansion_triggers: Same task name, action command, binary path, or hash appears on another host.

wmi-persistence.title: Permanent WMI event persistence
wmi-persistence.objective: Identify suspicious WMI event filters, consumers, bindings, queries, or command lines used for persistence and execution.
wmi-persistence.selection_guidance: Use when WMI consumers, event filters, suspicious namespaces, or WMI-launched commands are observed.

artifacts.notes: Zero rows on mapped dead-disk clients are not a clearing condition.

expected_signals: CommandLineEventConsumer launches script interpreters or suspicious paths
Filter and consumer names do not match installed enterprise software
Queries trigger on logon, process creation, or short recurring intervals
Consumer command correlates with suspicious binary or script evidence
caveats: Live WMI artifacts can be weak or unavailable on mapped dead-disk clients.
Consumer names and namespaces require environment context.
scope_expansion_triggers: Same consumer, filter, command, script path, or binary hash appears elsewhere.

rdp-or-explicit-logon-lateral-movement.title: RDP or explicit-credential lateral movement
rdp-or-explicit-logon-lateral-movement.objective: Identify remote interactive access or explicit credential use that moves between systems or launches remote administration.
rdp-or-explicit-logon-lateral-movement.selection_guidance: Use when source IPs, target accounts, RDP events, explicit logons, or remote-service activity are present.

artifacts.notes: Normalize DomainName and UserName but retain source fields.
Correlate subject, target, process, and server; no one field is sufficient.
Use as evidence of service-based movement adjacent to authentication.

expected_signals: New or unusual source IP authenticates to a target host
Explicit credential use targets another server
Remote logon followed by service creation, task execution, or PowerShell
Same account moves through several hosts in a short interval
benign_explanations: Jump hosts and privileged access workstations
caveats: Source IP may represent NAT, VPN, jump-host, or proxy infrastructure.
Explicit logon events require process and target-server context.
Administrator activity can resemble lateral movement.
scope_expansion_triggers: Same source IP or account authenticates to additional hosts.
Authentication is followed by service, task, WMI, or PowerShell execution.

suspicious-binary-execution.title: Suspicious binary presence and execution
suspicious-binary-execution.objective: Correlate file identity, execution-adjacent artifacts, signer metadata, and repeated host presence for a suspicious binary.
suspicious-binary-execution.selection_guidance: Use after a filename, path, hash, signer anomaly, or execution lead is identified.

artifacts.notes: Treat Amcache as presence and metadata evidence, not universal proof of execution.
Prefetch may be disabled, aged out, or absent.
BAM availability and retention depend on Windows version and state.
Use only after a bounded file lead exists.

expected_signals: Same path or hash appears across execution artifacts
Unsigned or unexpectedly signed executable
Binary runs from user-writable, temporary, or staging locations
Compile time, version metadata, imports, or PDB path conflict with claimed software
caveats: Presence and execution are distinct claims.
Timestamp semantics differ by artifact.
File identity should be confirmed with BinaryHunter or equivalent exact-path collection.
scope_expansion_triggers: Same hash, normalized path, signer anomaly, or PDB path appears on another host.

downloaded-payload-execution.title: Downloaded payload followed by execution
downloaded-payload-execution.objective: Correlate Mark-of-the-Web or download metadata with file creation and subsequent execution evidence.
downloaded-payload-execution.selection_guidance: Use when Zone.Identifier, browser download, suspicious URL, or newly created executable evidence exists.

artifacts.notes: Zone.Identifier can be absent or removed.
Use raw MFT for exact timestamp and path confirmation.
Use as application or execution-style context, not sole proof.

expected_signals: Untrusted or uncommon download domain
Executable or script downloaded into a user-writable location
Downloaded file is followed by Prefetch, BAM, Amcache, or PowerShell activity
Same payload hash or URL appears on multiple hosts
caveats: Mark-of-the-Web can be missing, stripped, or propagated inconsistently.
A downloaded file is not necessarily executed.
URLs may contain sensitive tokens and should be handled carefully.
scope_expansion_triggers: Same URL, domain, filename, path, or hash appears elsewhere.

archive-staging-or-exfiltration.title: Archive staging or endpoint-visible exfiltration
archive-staging-or-exfiltration.objective: Identify archive creation, staging directories, unusual outbound application usage, removable or shared destinations, and transfer-related activity.
archive-staging-or-exfiltration.selection_guidance: Use when archive utilities, large staged files, cloud-storage paths, unusual network usage, or transfer tooling are observed.

artifacts.notes: Use bounded path, extension, size, and time filters.
Review component-specific SRUM exports; fields vary by component.

expected_signals: Large archive created shortly before transfer-related activity
Archive or staging path under temporary, public, profile, or cloud-sync directories
Unusual application network usage near staging activity
Cloud-storage, browser, removable-media, or network-share context
caveats: SRUM provides usage context rather than packet-level proof of exfiltration.
Large archives and cloud synchronization are common business activity.
File size and timestamp evidence must be correlated with user and process context.
scope_expansion_triggers: Same archive name, staging path, cloud destination, transfer tool, or account appears on another host.

removable-media-or-network-share-use.title: Removable media or network-share usage
removable-media-or-network-share-use.objective: Identify user and host interaction with removable volumes, mounted shares, or external storage relevant to ingress, staging, or exfiltration.
removable-media-or-network-share-use.selection_guidance: Use when drive letters, volume identifiers, UNC paths, MountPoints2 data, or device-history evidence is relevant.

artifacts.notes: Field names remain unprofiled and require validation against live output.
Use for adjacent file activity on the local system.

expected_signals: Previously unseen removable volume or share
Mount activity near suspicious file creation or execution
Sensitive files staged before removable-media or share interaction
Same share, volume, or user appears across multiple hosts
caveats: Registry mount evidence does not prove a specific file transfer.
Shared infrastructure requires user and time correlation.
Dead-disk evidence may not establish current device state.
scope_expansion_triggers: Same share, removable volume, filename, or user activity appears on another host.

account-creation-or-privilege-change.title: Account creation or privilege change
account-creation-or-privilege-change.objective: Identify new accounts, group membership changes, privilege assignments, or suspicious use of newly modified identities.
account-creation-or-privilege-change.selection_guidance: Use when account-management events, new local users, administrator-group changes, or unusual privileged identities are observed.

artifacts.notes: Use explicit event-id and time bounds.
Use to determine whether a new or changed account was subsequently used.

expected_signals: New account followed by logon or explicit credential use
Unexpected addition to local or domain privileged groups
Password reset or account enablement by an unusual actor
Same newly created account appears on multiple systems
caveats: Account events require actor, target, host, and approval context.
Domain and local account semantics differ.
Registry account state does not provide complete domain history.
scope_expansion_triggers: New or modified identity authenticates to additional hosts.
Privilege change is followed by persistence or remote execution.
